summary: Ryōkei Kaginushi (1926–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He taught Nobuyoshi Yamabe and held professorships at Otani University, attested in 1978 and from 1987 to 1993.

Ryūshō Hikata (1892–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu (~1914–1917), taught Hiromasa Tosaki, and held posts at Kyushu University (~1925–1958) and Fukuoka Women's University (~1955–1963).
Ryūō Asahi (1856–1926) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who taught at Toji and Koyasan University.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar (1871–1946) was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Madras (~1890–1899), where he later served as Chair of Indian History and Archæology (~1914–1929).

S. Kuppuswami Sastri (1880–1943), a scholar of Indology and philosophy, founded the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras. He was Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (~1915–1935) and held professorships at Presidency University Kolkata, Presidency College Chennai (~1914–1935), and Annamalai University (~1936–1943).

S. N. Balagangadhara (born 1952) is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University, where he later served as Professor in Comparative Science of Cultures and research centre director (~1991–2017).
S. N. Savadi is an Indology scholar who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri (1893–1942) was a scholar in philosophy and Indology who held positions at the University of Madras as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and Department Head (attested 1942).

S. Sankaranarayanan (1926–2014) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He was an Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1986–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

Sabine Löhr is an Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing her doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen. She also served as a Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft at the University of Hamburg.

Sadahiko Kariya is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (attested 1977) and as a professor of Buddhist studies at Chizan Senmon Gakko (attested 2001).

Sadajiro Sugiura (1871–1947) worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rikkyo University (~1891–1893) and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~1898–1900), later holding a post at Rikkyo University.
Saileswar Sen worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Calcutta until 1920 and completed doctoral research under Barend Faddegon.
Sakda Hemthep is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MPhil at Cardiff University by 2014, supervised by Max Deeg.

Sakya Trizin (born 1945) is a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Appey, Tritsho Khenpo Rinchen, and the 14th Dalai Lama, and taught Steven Neal Weinberger, Sam van Schaik, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, Jared Rhoton, and Thutop Tulku.

Sakyong Mipham (born 1962) works in Buddhist and religious studies. The successor to Chögyam Trungpa, he studied under Trungpa, Khenpo Namdrol, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (~1987–1991), and Penor Rinpoche, and taught Pema Chödrön.

Sallie B. King (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (~1973–1981) and served as a professor (~1990–2014) and Professor Emerita at James Madison University.

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at UC Berkeley (PhD 1979) under Shivaram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri, later holding a post at UC Berkeley (attested 1996) and teaching Travis L. Smith and Jinah Kim.
Sally McAra specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000) under the supervision of Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.

Sally Mellick Cutler is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1993 and served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1997).
